content.title: About
content.content: Canned pineapple (NFS) consists of bite‑size pieces of ripe pineapple that have been hot‑sterilized and sealed in glass or metal jars with their own syrup. The product retains the sweet‑tart flavor and characteristic tropical aroma of fresh pineapple.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pineapple contains bromelain, an enzyme that helps break down proteins.
Canning allows pineapple to be stored for 2‑3 years without loss of taste or nutrients.
In the United States pineapple is a symbol of hospitality and is often served in cocktails and desserts.
The syrup left after canning is rich in vitamin C and B1 and can be used in cooking.
Pineapple was first introduced to Europe in the 16th century by Portuguese explorers.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis, promoting healthy skin.

items.title: Contains bromelain
items.content: Bromelain improves digestion, reduces inflammation, and may help muscle recovery after exercise.

items.title: Source of manganese
items.content: Manganese is involved in carbohydrate metabolism and fatty‑acid synthesis.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned pineapple contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports normal bowel function and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The syrup may contain added sugar, which is important for people managing diabetes.

items.title: Bromelain allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bromelain, such as swelling or itching.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may include preservatives (e.g., potassium sorbate); those with sensitivities should choose preservative‑free options.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of pineapple can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned pineapple can be enjoyed as a snack, added to fruit salads, yogurts, smoothies, baked goods, or used in sauces for meat and seafood. Before use, shake the jar well and drain excess syrup if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the pineapple in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
